newsitem.title: EGYPT: Amriyah sale boosts Egypt share prices.
newsitem.headline: Amriyah sale boosts Egypt share prices.

text.p: The sale of 1.822 million shares in Amriyah Cement to big investors boosted Egyptian share prices on Monday but the slow holiday season held back most other stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 2.96 points to 291.85. The Amriyah sale accounted for almost 86 million pounds ($25.30 million) of the high closing volume of 143.66 million.
The state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries sold the Amriyah Cement on Monday at 67.00 pounds, the minimum price in an auction earlier this month.
The operation at the Egyptian stock exchange was the second stage in the sale of about 3.4 million shares, 17 percent of Amriyah Cement's total equity.
The holding company sold close to one million of the shares on Sunday at between 67.01 and 71.00 pounds. The sale is expected to continue on Tuesday.
Amriyah was the day's most active share but fell 2.25 pounds to end trading at 66.00.
"It was a very shallow market today with limited prices. But we're on the edge of a new boom," said Mohammed Magdi with EFG/Hermes brokerage.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the biggest gainer for the second day in a row, rising 29.74 percent to 383.00.
Magdi said stock exchange officials had imposed a ceiling on Medinet Nasr because it felt brokers were overpricing the stock. He said he heard two ceiling prices -- 383 and 387 pounds.
The state sold its majority in Medinet Nasr eight months ago and shares were priced at 60 pounds each.
Bourse officials have frozen the price of another realty firm, Heliopolis Housing and Development at 430 pounds until a CMAcommittee investigates claims that the stock is overpriced.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 440.76 points from 432.44 points on Sunday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 204.75 from 202.62.
